§C.11 Ground Truth — Tables 4-8

Working steps for annotators producing ground truth for tables: columns, rows and cells, cell values, titles and edges, and special table types. Each step serves the rule it links to; the rule decides what the output is.

Structure before styling

  1. Read the table's structure first — rows, columns, header tiers — ignoring weight and slant. Then go cell by cell and mark bold, italic and underline only where the glyphs show it. → Bold and Italic Inside Tables§9.6.2
  2. Read each row's level from where its label starts in the stub, never from the numbers. → Row-Label Hierarchy§9.5.5
  3. Where a total's printed indent contradicts the grouping it sums, keep the printed level and add a review note describing the conflict. → Total and Subtotal Rows§9.5.6

Evidence, not eyeballing

  1. For a column of identical values, extract the word boxes and read their coordinates: one occurrence means a rowspan, distinct positions mean separate cells. → Repeated Identical Values§9.5.4
  2. Settle a disputed digit from a zoomed crop or the word coordinates, never from the text layer. → Cell Text Fidelity§9.6.3
  3. Decide from the image which glyphs are printed and which are handwritten or stamped. → Handwriting and Stamps§9.6.5
  4. After finding one struck-through cell, re-check the whole column at zoom. Flagging a redline table is done in addition to that check, never instead of it. → Struck and Replaced Values§9.6.7

Flag for review

  1. Flag any page where a header/body column-count mismatch was repaired by padding with empty cells. → Header Body Column Count Mismatch§9.4.2
  2. Flag pages whose icon vocabulary needed a judgement call. → Marks and Symbols in Cells§9.6.6
  3. Where a table's frame is ambiguous (what belongs at its bottom edge), flag the page and record the encoding chosen for the document. → Bottom Edge Totals and Islands§9.7.1
  4. Record once per document whether section-divider bands are bold <td> or <th>, and apply it on every page. → Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3
  5. Place a footnote by its marker, not by where the frame happens to be drawn. → Footnotes Inside the Frame§9.7.2

Older annotations

  1. A $ kept in its own column track as a spanned pair in an existing annotation is not wrong and need not be redone; new work puts the symbol in the value's cell. → Gutter Columns§9.4.1
